Root cause of the false alarm: this session's (and every prior session's) local clone of jobfynder-docs is shallow with the create_session default clone_depth of 50 (confirmed via `git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` + `.git/shallow` in this run), so `git rev-list --count origin/main` on any fresh session's clone will always read exactly ~50 and `b90b437`/whatever sits at that boundary will always look like a parentless orphan root locally -- that is an artifact of the clone, not of the remote repository. Checked directly against GitHub: b90b437 (check #129) has parent 40500e21d5d694620717e20999c5c14ea1287cea (check #128, cited since check #170 as 'garbage-collected' -- it is not; GitHub returns it normally), which has parent 1e0807d7... (check #127), and so on continuously; cc59fc75 (PR #59's base commit, 2026-10-19) is confirmed reachable from current main via the GitHub commits API. There was no force-push, no truncation, and no loss of history; PRs #59-#62 are ordinary open PRs with no ancestry problem. The claim should not be repeated. (Separately, checks #128-171 were themselves correct that `cbfda976...` is an ordinary mid-history commit, not a root -- that part stands, it just was never evidence of an incident in the first place.) No doc content under JOBFYNDER-HERMES-COMM-CANONICAL.md, hermes/*.md or comm/*.md ever cited this finding, so no documentation correction is needed beyond this state file. Human attention item going forward is just the real one: PRs #59-#62 open 8-54 days with no human activity, per the existing re-escalation mechanism -- not a git-integrity incident.
